Optimal.Notes: Civ V runs comfortably at native resolution and high settings on the Deck; the 40 Hz refresh and frame cap keep power use balanced and eliminate screen tearing. AI processing time on large maps is the real bottleneck, not graphics.
Optimal.ExpectedFps: 40 fps (stable during gameplay; AI turns cause waits)

profiles.Summary: Civilization V is a 2010 turn-based strategy game with very modest GPU demands, running natively on Linux via Aspyr's port, and the Steam Deck handles it with ease even at higher settings. The main performance concern is late-game CPU overhead from AI calculations on large maps, not GPU load.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the 2010 PC minimum/recommended requirements (well below Deck capability) and the known Linux native port by Aspyr. On first run, check that the Aspyr native Linux version launches correctly — if unstable, switch to Proton Experimental. Watch for AI turn stall times on large maps late in a game.

MaxBattery.Notes: This game is extremely light on the GPU; the TDP and clock limits here are primarily to save battery during long sessions. AI turn processing is CPU-bound and unavoidable regardless of graphics settings.
MaxBattery.ExpectedFps: 30-40 fps (GPU-bound turns); CPU stalls during AI turns

KnownIssues: Late-game turns on large maps with many civilizations can cause significant CPU stall/hang time, reducing effective frame rate regardless of GPU settings.
The Linux (Aspyr) native build may have occasional audio or stability quirks; running via Proton can sometimes be more stable.
UI text and interface elements may appear small at native 1280x800 without scaling adjustments in the in-game interface options.
No native Steam Deck controller layout is officially provided; community layouts or mouse-trackpad input are recommended.

MaxPerformance.Notes: The Deck GPU far exceeds Civ V's recommended specs, so Ultra settings at native resolution are achievable; the main frame-rate interruptions are AI-turn CPU stalls on large maps with many civs, which no GPU setting can fix.
MaxPerformance.ExpectedFps: 55-60 fps during player turns; drops during AI processing

Optimal.Notes: The Deck GPU far exceeds this game's recommended spec, so native 1280x800 with high textures and terrain detail runs smoothly; FSR is unnecessary. Battery dips toward the lower end during late-game large-map sessions due to sustained CPU AI load.

profiles.Summary: Civilization V is a 2010 turn-based strategy game that the Steam Deck handles comfortably from a GPU standpoint, easily exceeding recommended PC specs. The primary performance concern is CPU-bound AI processing during late-game turns on large maps, which causes periodic stalls regardless of graphics settings.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were found; profiles are estimated from the 2010 PC minimum/recommended requirements against the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU (well above the recommended spec). On first run, verify UI text is readable at 1280x800, set up a Steam Input community layout for controls, and watch for AI-turn stall frequency on your chosen map size.

MaxBattery.Notes: At 6 W TDP this 2010 title is GPU-idle most of the time; disabling leader scene animations removes the biggest GPU spike and keeps frame pacing consistent. Battery life is dominated by CPU load during AI turns rather than rendering.

KnownIssues: Late-game AI turn processing on large maps causes multi-second stalls that cannot be resolved by lowering graphics settings — this is a CPU/engine limitation.
No native gamepad support; a Steam Input community layout is required for comfortable handheld play.
Some UI text and interface elements can appear small at the native 1280x800 resolution, contributing to the Playable (not Verified) rating.
Occasional hangs or crashes on exit have been reported under Proton, though in-session stability is generally good.

MaxPerformance.Notes: This 2010 engine is not GPU-limited at max settings on the Deck, so frame rates will be high during panning and idle turns; AI-processing stalls are a CPU/engine ceiling and will occur regardless of any graphics setting.
